o: Exhortations to add the exercise of various other graces to faith.
The apostle looks forward to his approaching decease.
And confirms the truth of the gospel, relating to Christ's appearing to judgment.
bg: The question of the authenticity of this epistle has been much discussed, but the weight of evidence is wholly in favour of its claim to be the production of the apostle whose name it bears. It appears to have been written shortly before the apostle's death (1:14). This epistle contains eleven references to the Old Testament.
ch.s: This chapter covers: Exhortations to add the exercise of various other graces to faith (vv. 1–11); The apostle looks forward to his approaching decease (vv. 12–15); And confirms the truth of the gospel, relating to Christ's appearing to judgment (vv. 16–21). People named: Simon, Peter.
ch.mh: Faith unites the weak believer to Christ, as really as it does the strong one, and purifies the heart of one as truly as of another; and every sincere believer is by his faith justified in the sight of God.
q: Read verses 1–11 (Exhortations to add the exercise of various other graces to faith). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 12–15 (The apostle looks forward to his approaching decease), what do you learn about wisdom?
Verse 3 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside 1 Peter 5:10. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Simon’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of holiness in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 2 Peter?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: We must be established in the belief of the truth, that we may not be shaken by every wind of doctrine; and especially in the truth necessary for us to know in our day, what belongs to our peace, and what is opposed in our time.
ch.a: Before a decision this week, pause and ask what this chapter would counsel.

o: Believers are cautioned against false teachers, and the certainty of their punishment shown from examples.
An account of these seducers, as exceedingly wicked.
But as making high pretences to liberty and purity.
bg: The question of the authenticity of this epistle has been much discussed, but the weight of evidence is wholly in favour of its claim to be the production of the apostle whose name it bears. It appears to have been written shortly before the apostle's death (1:14). This epistle contains eleven references to the Old Testament.

Burning; the walled, a city in the vale of Siddim (Gen. 13:10; 14:1-16). The wickedness of its inhabitants brought down upon it fire from heaven, by which it was destroyed (18:16-33; 19:1-29; Deut. 23:17).

He lived five hundred years, and then there were born unto him three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth (Gen. 5:32). He was a "just man and perfect in his generation," and "walked with God" (comp. Ezek. 14:14, 20).

Lot, (Heb. lot), a covering; veil, the son of Haran, and nephew of Abraham (Gen. 11:27). On the death of his father, he was left in charge of his grandfather Terah (31), after whose death he accompanied his uncle Abraham into Canaan (12:5), thence into Egypt (10), and back again to Canaan (13:1). ch.s: This chapter covers: Believers are cautioned against false teachers, and the certainty of their punishment shown from examples (vv. 1–9); An account of these seducers, as exceedingly wicked (vv. 10–16); But as making high pretences to liberty and purity (vv. 17–22). People named: Noah, Lot, Balaam. Places: Sodom.
ch.mh: Though the way of error is a hurtful way, many are always ready to walk therein.
q: Read verses 1–9 (Believers are cautioned against false teachers, and the certainty of their punishment shown from examples). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 10–16 (An account of these seducers, as exceedingly wicked), what do you learn about judgment?
Verse 1 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Matthew 7:15. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Noah’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of salvation and redemption in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 2 Peter?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: Let us take care we give no occasion to the enemy to blaspheme the holy name whereby we are called, or to speak evil of the way of salvation by Jesus Christ, who is the Way, the Truth, and the Life.
ch.a: Let the seriousness of God's judgment move you to examine your ways and to pray for others.

o: The design here is to remind of Christ's final coming to judgement.
He will appear unexpectedly, when the present frame of nature will be dissolved by fire.
From thence is inferred the need for holiness, and stedfastness in the faith.
bg: The question of the authenticity of this epistle has been much discussed, but the weight of evidence is wholly in favour of its claim to be the production of the apostle whose name it bears. It appears to have been written shortly before the apostle's death (1:14). This epistle contains eleven references to the Old Testament.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The design here is to remind of Christ's final coming to judgement (vv. 1–4); He will appear unexpectedly, when the present frame of nature will be dissolved by fire (vv. 5–10); From thence is inferred the need for holiness, and stedfastness in the faith (vv. 11–18). People named: Paul.
ch.mh: The purified minds of Christians are to be stirred up, that they may be active and lively in the work of holiness.
q: Read verses 1–4 (The design here is to remind of Christ's final coming to judgement). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 5–10 (He will appear unexpectedly, when the present frame of nature will be dissolved by fire), what do you learn about holiness?
Verse 9 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside 1 Timothy 2:4. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Paul’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of wisdom in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 2 Peter?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: And that we may avoid being led away, we must seek to grow in all grace, in faith, and virtue, and knowledge.
ch.a: Before a decision this week, pause and ask what this chapter would counsel.
